messages:
maia liu: quick sync — i'm putting together the UX for automatic handoff policies (what we call 'safeguard handoff'). need alignment on modes, triggers, and what we surface in the audit playback. who can weigh in?

alex park: +1. IDEA: expose 3 modes in the console: `transparent` (route + keep orig), `degrade` (route to cheaper variant), `quarantine` (reject and queue). keep names short.

kevin ong: agree on modes. triggers should be pluggable: `5xx_rate`, `latency_p95`, `gpu_oom`, and `quota_exhaustion`. also support compound rules (e.g. `5xx_rate>3% && p95>500ms`).

jordan s.: telemetry needs: event id, policy_version, trigger_reason, decision_path (why route to X), and a sampling of the request payload (redacted). audit playback should be able to replay request -> decision -> resulting model output.

sam khan: UI suggestions: timeline card that shows: policy version, active window, short diff of changed rules, and a simulate button that runs N synthetic requests and shows probability of each mode firing. also an inline `why` hover that shows the last matching rule.

maia liu: for quota_exhaustion, do we prefer to route to a smaller model or reject with a clear error? product tradeoffs?

alex park: product view: prefer degrade to smaller model for PLG routes; for enterprise routes allow strict reject toggle (customer can opt-in). add per-route fallback budget so we can limit spillover.

kevin ong: implementation note: routing should be atomic per request. when policy triggers, emit a `handoff.trace_id` and attach `policy_snapshot` to the output so downstream can correlate. we also need a TTL for policy-only cache so changes don't cause weird mid-request flips.

maia liu: sounds good. how granular is the audit capture? full token stream or sampled?

jordan s.: sampled by default. store hashed prompt + redaction marker for PII. for high-severity events (large error spikes) we capture full de-identified payloads. retention policy controlled by workspace settings.

sam khan: UX for rollouts — have `automatic` vs `manual` toggle. automatic mode can do `canary %` for the first N hours and then escalate. include a small badge: "policy active since X" and a link to `playback` which opens a sandbox.

maia liu: need one-off emergency escape: a global "stop-handovers" toggle that ops can flip which forces all routes to original model. should appear in console header.

alex park: +1. also expose an audit export (CSV/JSON) filtered by timeframe, route, policy_version. customers will ask for this for compliance.

kevin ong: quick proto of minimal policy shape (for the API):
```json
{
  "mode": "quarantine",
  "triggers": [{"type":"5xx_rate","threshold":0.03},{"type":"p95_latency","threshold_ms":500}],
  "route_to": "model-small-v1",
  "canary_pct": 5,
  "audit": true
}
```

maia liu: good sample. for `audit: true` what level of detail?

audit-bot: [system] captured event: ts=3267890139 id=hb-89c3 policy_version=2 trigger=5xx_rate reason="5.1% in 1m" route_to=model-small-v1

jordan s.: include `pre_hand_off_metrics` snapshot (active connections, qps, queued) in the audit event so playback can simulate realistic load.

sam khan: also we should show cost delta estimate when proposing a route change (e.g. "expected cost -23% / latency +150ms"), so teams can weigh tradeoffs in the UI.

maia liu: one last question — how do we handle multi-route requests (batching across models)?

kevin ong: policy evaluation per-request key. batching may combine outputs; we should annotate batch-level audit with per-item decision. if we route some items to fallback, the batch response should include `item_decisions: [orig, handoff, orig]`.

alex park: next steps: sam will mock the console card + simulate flow, kevin will draft API shape & tracing headers, jordan will spec telemetry fields and sampling, i'll write product acceptance criteria.

sam khan: i'll have a clickable prototype by next Wed. :calendar:

maia liu: perfect. thanks all. i'll create the RFC PR and include the sample policy JSON above.
